did.abstract: Ruth Gruber (1911-2016) was a photojournalist, humanitarian, author, and lecturer from Brooklyn, New York. Gruber was a foreign correspondent for the New York Herald Tribune, where she wrote about women under fascism, the Soviet Arctic, and two humanitarian missions involving the escort of Jewish refugees and survivors of the Holocaust. In 1941, she was hired by the U.S. Department of the Interior to report on aspects of the former Alaska Territory. She also wrote for the New York Post, Hadassah Magazine and other periodicals and newspapers. Gruber wrote 19 books based on her experiences as a journalist, as well as on her advocacy for Jewish refugees and the state of Israel after World War II. The Ruth Gruber Papers consist of photographs, slides, correspondence, and writings from approximately 1922 to 2016, related to her personal and professional life. Gruber's personal life is reflected through her correspondence, photographs, writing, and home movies. Gruber's work as a photojournalist and writer from circa 1932 to 2011, and her study of the former Alaska Territory while employed as a Department of Interior Field Representative, are reflected through her articles, notebooks, manuscripts, photographs, audio and video recordings, and correspondence. Her humanitarian efforts are chronicled through her notebooks, photographs, writing, and interviews.

bioghist.head: Biographical Note
bioghist.p: Ruth Gruber (1911-2016) was a photojournalist, humanitarian, author, and lecturer from Brooklyn, New York. Born to a family of Russian Jewish immigrants, she enrolled at New York University at the age of 15. She completed a postgraduate fellowship at the University of Wisconsin and earned her PhD from the University of Cologne in Cologne, Germany in 1932, becoming one of the youngest women in the world to receive a doctorate. Gruber was a foreign correspondent for the New York Herald Tribune, where she wrote about women under fascism and traveled to the Soviet Arctic. In 1941, she was hired by the U.S. Department of the Interior to report on aspects of the former Alaska Territory. In 1944, she worked on a classified wartime mission to escort one thousand Jewish refugees from Naples, Italy, into the U.S. at Fort Ontario, helping oversee and advocate for their permanent settlement in Oswego, New York. In July 1947, at the Port of Haifa, Gruber covered the events involving British warships intercepting a steamship called Exodus 1947 which transported 4,515 refugees and survivors of the Holocaust. As a correspondent for the New York Herald Tribune and the New York Post, she covered the work of the Anglo-American Committee of Inquiry on Palestine and the United Nations Special Committee on Palestine (UNSCOP), focusing primarily on the permanent settlement of European Jewish refugees living in refugee camps. In 1951, Gruber began writing a column called "Diary of an American Housewife" in Hadassah Magazine. Gruber wrote 19 books based on her experiences as a journalist, as well as on her advocacy for Jewish refugees and the state of Israel after World War II. She received five honorary doctorates and many other honors and recognitions, including the International Center of Photography's Infinity Award, awards from the Simon Wiesenthal Center's Museum of Tolerance, and others specifically for her books. Gruber died on November 17, 2016, at the age of 105. Throughout her seventy years as a journalist and humanitarian, as she states in her 2007 memoir, Witness, she was inspired to "record...the truth of whatever I was witnessing, no matter how controversial it might be" (Ruth Gruber, Witness: One of the Great Correspondents of the Twentieth Century Tells Her Story, [Schocken Books, 2007], 97).

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: Before transfer to NYU Library, materials were packed and an inventory was created by those administering Gruber's estate. While still at Gruber's home, a portion of the material was repacked by NYU staff into more appropriately-sized containers, which changed the content description of the original inventory. Changes were notated when possible.

In 2018, at the time of accessioning, three graduate student workers rehoused material into archival boxes and folders when necessary. The boxes were renumbered and a new box level inventory was created. A column was included in the spreadsheet, notating original inventory box numbers/letters when possible. The material was inventoried to the box-level. Born-digital items were separated from the material, boxed, labeled, and inventoried in Medialog.
In November 2023, an accretion of photographs and issues of the Ontario Chronicle were rehoused in archival folders and added to the collection's inventory.

At the time of processing in 2026, the collection was arranged and described into series. Materials were placed into acid-free manuscript boxes and folders, and oversized materials were rehoused in appropriately sized boxes. Items were removed from non-archival sleeves. Duplicate publications and documents, publications widely available online or in NYU's catalog holdings, and documents with sensitive personal information were removed. All negatives and slides were rehoused into corresponding archival sleeves. Some photographs were rehoused in Mylar sleeves. Forty-seven individually rolled negatives were flattened by Preservation and rehoused in archival negative sleeves.

89 CDs, DVDs, floppy disks, and zip disks were forensically imaged, analyzed, and arranged in Forensic Toolkit. New York University Libraries follow professional standards and best practices when imaging, ingesting, and processing born-digital material in order to maintain the integrity and authenticity of the content.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The Ruth Gruber Papers (bulk 1930-2014) consist of photographs, slides, correspondence, and writings related to her personal and professional life. Gruber's personal life is reflected through her correspondence, photographs, slides, notebooks, and travel ephemera. Her educational experiences as an undergraduate student at New York University during the 1920s and PhD studies at the University of Cologne in Germany during the 1930s are represented through writings, notebooks, and correspondence. Gruber's work as a photojournalist and foreign correspondent from approximately 1932 to 2011 is reflected through her articles, notebooks, manuscripts, and correspondence generated while working for the New York Herald Tribune, the New York Post, and other publications. Additionally, this collection contains photographs, slides, audio and video recordings, electronic records, and digital images related to her journalistic work. Correspondence, travel documents, notebooks, films, slides, and photographs from 1941 to 1945 document Gruber's study of the former Alaska Territory. Her participation in the escorting of one thousand Jewish refugees to Fort Ontario in Oswego, New York in 1944, as well as her coverage of the Jewish refugees aboard Exodus 1947, are chronicled through her notebooks, photographs, clippings, and interviews. Gruber's books are documented through drafts, galleys, correspondence with publishers, reviews, research materials, slides, photographs, and screen and theater adaptations. Publications represented in the collection include Haven: The Dramatic Story of 1,000 World War II Refugees and How They Came to America, Exodus 1947: The Ship That Launched the Nation, and Witness: One of the Great Correspondents of the Twentieth Century Tells Her Story. All of the materials in this collection reflect Gruber's humanitarian approach to journalism, her role as a female foreign correspondent, the development of Alaska pre-statehood, and the formation of Israel.

phystech.head: Born-Digital Access Policies and Procedures
phystech.p: Advance notice is required for the use of computer records. Original physical digital media is restricted. An access terminal for born-digital materials in the collection is available by appointment for reading room viewing and listening only. Researchers may view an item's original container and/or carrier, but the physical carriers themselves are not available for use because of preservation concerns.

phystech.head: Audiovisual Access Policies and Procedures
phystech.p: Some audiovisual materials have not been preserved and may not be available to researchers. Materials not yet digitized will need to have access copies made before they can be used. To request an access copy, or if you are unsure if an item has been digitized, please contact NYU Special Collections (special.collections@nyu.edu, 212-998-2596) with the collection name, collection number, and a description of the item(s) requested. A staff member will respond to you with further information.

userestrict.head: Conditions Governing Use
userestrict.p: This collection is protected by copyright and/or related rights. You are free to use materials in the collection in any way that is permitted by the copyright and related rights legislation that applies to your use. For other uses you need to obtain permission from the rights-holder(s).

custodhist.head: Custodial History
custodhist.p: Prior to acquisition, the materials in the November 2023 accretion had been separated from the Gruber collection and loaned to the United States Holocaust Museum for exhibition.

appraisal.head: Appraisal
appraisal.p: Forty-seven cartons of paper were appraised out of the collection during processing, including duplicates and items considered out of scope of the collection (financial documents, travel itineraries and tickets, health records, diplomas, book contracts and loan agreements, and records of Gruber's spouses). Four cartons of audiovisual material and computer disks were also removed from the collection, many of which were off-air recordings. Off-air recordings, in both analog and digital formats, were appraised out of the collection due to copyright limitations. These recordings include commercial musical and video recordings and any recordings from a copyrighted broadcast or television transmission.

relatedmaterial.head: Related Materials
relatedmaterial.p: Additional archival collections on Ruth Gruber are held at the the Henry W. and Albert A. Berg Collection of English and American Literature at the New York Public Library, the Virginia Holocaust Museum, and the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains materials related to Gruber's personal and family life. Materials cover awards, education, teaching, volunteering, and writing. Included are photographs and films in analog and digital formats of Gruber and her family; family and general correspondence; and travel slides, videos, and films. Also included in this series are daily planners, teaching materials from courses mostly taught at Hunter College, correspondence and event flyers related to organizations for which she volunteered, press and publicity, marriage and divorce certificates, and an oral history recording and corresponding transcript. Gruber's early writing is not only reflected in the journals, poetry, essays, and short stories included here, but in the papers written throughout her academic life. Of note are the files related to her PhD dissertation on Virginia Woolf, completed at the University of Cologne; the thesis was published in 1935 and is considered one of the first feminist interpretations of Woolf's writing and life.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series consists of materials related to Gruber's career as a foreign correspondent for newspapers, such as New York Herald Tribune, the New York Post, and The New York Times, and periodicals, including Hadassah Magazine, Look, and The New Republic. Also included are materials related to Gruber's work in Alaska as Harold L. Ickes's field representative with the Department of the Interior, for which she wrote governmental reports and articles based on her experiences. Gruber's eyewitness accounts on the Soviet Arctic and Alaska, Jewish refugees during World War II, European refugee camps, the March on Washington, Jewish Ethiopian refugees, and the social and political changes in Puerto Rico since 1940 are reflected in her article drafts and manuscripts; correspondence; research material; lecture notes; notebooks; photographs, negatives, and slides; and press and publicity. Materials related to books published on Gruber's time in the Soviet Arctic and Alaska can be found in Series IV. Materials in this series reflect Gruber's journalistic efforts to focus on humanitarianism; the process of Alaska's transition from territory to statehood; the formation of the State of Israel; and the reality of being a woman in a male-dominated field.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Included in this subseries are materials related to Gruber's travels in the Soviet Arctic as a correspondent for the New York Herald Tribune, and her coverage of the work of the Anglo-American Committee of Inquiry on Palestine and the United Nations Special Committee on Palestine (UNSCOP) on behalf of both the New York Herald Tribune and the New York Post. This subseries consists of drafts of published articles; correspondence with publishers; research materials (articles and publications); photographs, negatives, and slides; and journals/notebooks. Also included are drafts and correspondence for articles with other publications, including The New York Times, The Jewish Week, and the North American Newspaper Alliance. Lectures and appearances related to her journalistic efforts are reflected in correspondence, programs and flyers, press, audio and video recordings in both analog and digital formats, drafts, notes, and notebooks.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries contains materials related to Gruber's work as a field representative for the Department of the Interior. Tasked with writing a social and economic study of Alaska, Gruber also wrote articles for New York Herald Tribune and other publications about her experiences. Materials consist of internal memos; drafts and notes for reports (most of which were written by Gruber but not all, such as the report on arts and crafts); final reports; correspondence; journals/notebooks; research materials on various topics (such as the Fish and Wildlife Service, Canol oil pipeline, and discrimination against Alaska Natives); photographs, slides, and negatives; drafts of articles; and film reels. Of note is the film, "Alaska: The New Frontier", which is an edited silent film accompanied by a scripted lecture about Alaska made by Gruber for the Department of the Interior. Included are the film in digital and analog formats, outtakes, and a script. Also of note, and a reflection of Gruber's commitment to documenting the Alaskan territory pre-statehood, are the large amount of slides, negatives, and photographic prints of the Alaska countryside, its people, and everyday life.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains materials related to Gruber's various humanitarian efforts. Most of the series pertains to the 1000 Jewish refugees who settled in Oswego, New York and the Jewish refugees aboard Exodus 1947, the two humanitarian rescue missions for which Gruber acted as an escort and witness. Also included are materials related to Holocaust remembrance events and the plight of Ethiopian Jews. Since this series focuses on these humanitarian events and Gruber's responsibility of documenting them, her photography and related exhibitions are included. Most of these photographs were subsequently used in her reporting and books. Materials consist of photographic prints, slides, and negatives; war relocation reports; passenger questionnaires; State Department documents; correspondence; journals/notebooks; committee reports and meeting minutes; writings by refugees; former refugee reunion photographs and correspondence; lecture notes, programs, and audio and video recordings, in both analog and digital formats; correspondence with former refugees and ship passengers; press and publicity on former refugees; and materials related to the establishments of the Oswego Italian Haven Scholarship and Safe Haven Museum. Exhibition materials (correspondence, catalogs, and lecture notes) of Gruber's photographs at various institutions, including the Museum of Jewish Heritage and the International Center of Photography, are also included. All of the materials in this series reflect Gruber's focus on rescue and sanctuary for the Jewish people.

arrangement.p: Arranged chronologically, with the exception of photography and photography exhibitions, which are located at the end.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series consists of materials related to Gruber's published books, unrealized books, and other writing projects, such as radio scripts and dramatic sketches. Each subseries contains one or more of the following: research materials; drafts; outlines; proposals; galleys; edit suggestions; publicity materials (book announcements, articles about Gruber, and interviews with Gruber); book reviews; fan mail; photographs (both analog and digital), negatives, and slides used in the final publications; event-related materials (lecture notes and announcements, book party invitations, conference programs, video and audio recordings, and photographs); notebooks and notes; adaptation materials (miniseries scripts and publicity; musical script and playbill); and scrapbooks, which mainly include publicity materials and photographs. These materials reflect Gruber's eyewitness approach to journalism, dedication to covering the formation of new nation-states and territories, and concentration on humanitarian efforts.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Arranged into 19 subseries, chronologically by publication date, followed by Scripts and Other Book-Related Projects and Unrealized Projects and Research alphabetically.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains materials related to topics (including antisemitism), individuals (such as Elie Wiesel), and organizations (including United Jewish Appeal, the American Jewish Joint Distribution Committee/JDC, and Youth Aliyah), of interest to Gruber and most likely used as research materials. Materials consist of articles, publications, audio and video recordings, and mailings.
